lead: A corner of the Eixample with a gentler pace, with its own national theatre, concert hall, market and library.
text: Its name comes from the Fuerte Pío, a fort that Philip V ordered built after 1714 and named after Captain General Francisco Pío de Saboya; the fort and the Citadel were demolished in 1869. In 1861 the railway station for the Lleida line was built here, giving identity to a neighbourhood between the railway tracks and Gran Via, and many hauliers settled beside the old Ribes road. The station closed in the last quarter of the 20th century, and today its building, extended in 1910 with a large iron roof, is the city's main bus station.

Next to the station an urban park was created and, on the other side, a complex with a nursery school, sheltered flats for the elderly, a market and a library, which the district itself presents as a model of how to integrate public facilities and public space. Today it is a residential neighbourhood, with the Teatre Nacional de Catalunya and L'Auditori as its great cultural landmarks. It is a good choice for anyone who wants the Eixample without the bustle of its major shopping avenues: quieter streets, local shops and the centre a walk away. At an average sale price of 4,806 €/m², it sits below La Dreta, L'Antiga Esquerra and La Nova Esquerra.
housing: Flats in buildings of the Cerdà grid, on streets with little traffic.
